## COCKPIT command: one fresh project thread per command

Measured on an adopting app with 0.40.0 (#105): every API fire of the COCKPIT command starts a fresh project thread,
whatever session the task is bound to; a task without the repository attached gets HTTP 403 on it; the fire text
arrives as `<routine-fire-payload>`, sometimes after the prompt; a thread read other open cockpit issues; issue writes
failed because cloud sessions refuse GraphQL; and the thread had the project's default connectors. 0.41.0 describes
the command as it works and replaces what 0.40.0 said about it.

### The COCKPIT command (`routines/cockpit-command.md`)

- **Every fire starts one fresh project thread**, the command thread for the one issue the command links. It carries
  that issue through the chain and the merge path, sends its start and its result to the coordinator (which runs the
  go and the merge as for any thread), then comments and closes the issue. Binding the task to the coordinator's
  session (`persistent_session_id`) is gone from the setup steps, and `routines/README.md` has no exception any more:
  every routine runs in a fresh session.
- **Setup:** the owner adds the API trigger **and attaches the project's repository with write access** in the web
  form. The setup is done only when the test fire reaches a thread that can read the repository: `COCKPIT test:`
  gets one line naming the main branch's head commit.
- **The payload:** the command is the content of `<routine-fire-payload>`, which can arrive as a separate message
  after the prompt; until it is there, the thread ends its turn without posting anything.
- **One issue only:** the thread acts only on the issue the payload links, never on other open `cockpit` issues.
- **Issue writes through REST:** comment, label and close go through `gh api` (`POST .../issues/<N>/comments`,
  `PATCH .../issues/<N> -f state=closed`), tried before reporting a missing permission, with the HTTP status reported
  when a call fails.
- **Connectors:** a task attached to a project gets the project's default connectors in every thread it starts; the
  brief tells the owner to remove them from the project's defaults if command threads should not have them.
- **New task prompt** carrying all of the above.

The managed `AGENTS.md` block (Cockpit issues), WORKFLOW §8.6 and §13, the README, the worktree manager and the
release gate (`validate.mjs`) say the same; the gate fails when the brief binds the task to a session or loses any of
these rules.

### Adopting projects

- **Replace the task prompt** of `<PROJECT> · COCKPIT command` with the new one from `routines/cockpit-command.md`
  (claude.ai/code/routines → the task → prompt).
- **Attach the project's repository with write access** to that task in the same web form, and save.
- Press Test in COCKPIT: the setup is done when a new project thread posts one line naming the main branch's head
  commit.

Install from npm: `npm i -D @softure-ai/skills@0.41.0`

Install from this release (no registry, no auth): `npm i -D https://github.com/SOFTURE/SKILLS/releases/download/v0.41.0/softure-ai-skills-0.41.0.tgz`

GitHub Packages: `@softure/skills@0.41.0` (requires a token with read:packages)
